items.title: 68642_Jo Jones oral history interview
items.q: so that's when Freddie Green joined the band, January 1937, and we were still at the Roseland Ballroom.

ctx.x: Buck Clayton, Walter Page, you know - what was this?

1937, I think it was around January 17th. Benny Goodman was jiving Joe Jackson because you know in those days you could not be under contract with somebody - yeh, 'Shoeless Joe Jackson,' that's what his name was. The first time that I ever met Mr. Freddie Green . He was down at the Black Cat place, so after we got through playing the recording it was decided that Claude should go back to Kansas City or Oklahoma or somewhere, so that's when Freddie Green joined the band, January 1937, and we were still at the…

items.title: 68097_Freddie Green oral history interview
items.q: But, I stayed out of the way -- now, because Jo Jones and Walter Page and Basie was doing something else.

ctx.x: Well, Freddie -- I mean -- that must have been -- I mean -- that really -- that was a rhythm section like there's never been a rhythm section like That in a band before.
I know, you know. But, I stayed out of the way -- now, because Jo Jones and Walter Page and Basie was doing something else. You see, I think --
You didn't stay out of the way -- you fell right in with them.
